first.rationale: Onboarding completion is currently down, and inherited evidence directly links shorter onboarding to faster time-to-value and higher completion, with related evidence that simplification durably improved SMB activation. This addresses the active funnel deterioration without adopting promotional pricing known to damage 30-day retention. Verify the two most directly relevant records, then run a guarded test with qualified-revenue and retention stop conditions because prior evidence does not yet establish long-term revenue impact.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, initially focused on SMB. The verified evidence directly addresses the current completion and activation declines: shorter onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification also increased activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%. Monitor retention and qualified revenue because signup simplification showed a 1% retention decline and its result did not replicate beyond SMB. Do not pursue competitor-matching promotional pricing given the inherited material retention harm.
